hardware: x86_64 Linux container, 4 vCPU, full Docker Compose stack (pipeline + observability profiles); not the target Mac
setup: 100,000 seeded vehicles; simulator at ~10,000 events/s; Prometheus v3.5.0 scraping every service; rules infra/monitoring/prometheus/rules/prognos.rules.yml
fault: docker compose stop detector (the only detector replica)

timeline_utc.targetdown_alert: never fired: Docker DNS discovery removes a stopped container from the target list, so there is no up == 0 series to alert on
timeline_utc.fix_applied: ServiceDown alert per job: absent(up{job="X"} == 1) for 2m; rules reloaded ~10:02

pipeline_falling_behind: not fired: detector was above 60 s behind from ~10:06:04 to ~10:10:40 (about 4.6 min), below the for: 5m clause; it was recovering the whole time
data_loss: none expected: the detector resumed from its committed Kafka offsets (Kafka retention 7 days); not separately reconciled in this drill
findings: TargetDown (up == 0) cannot detect a stopped service under DNS service discovery. Added ServiceDown (absent-based) alerts and a promtool test for them.
Seconds-behind right after a restart is overstated (peak 5,723 s) because the 5-minute consume rate still includes the down period. It converged within ~1 minute.
AlertLatencySLOBurn fired after the drain, because alerts raised from backlog events were minutes late relative to device time. The SLO saw the user-visible impact of the outage, as intended.
Found while screenshotting: the API availability stat showed 'No data' because the 5xx numerator has no series when there are no errors. Fixed with `or vector(0)` and a promtool test.
